_README: Provenance for every fixture in this directory. RECORDED = a real response from the live API. DERIVED = mechanically transformed from a recorded one. SYNTHETIC = written by hand, never seen from the API. A synthetic fixture can prove a detector works; it cannot prove the API behaves that way. bodySha256 makes a silent edit visible - pnpm fixtures:check recomputes and compares.

twelvedata-xauusd-15min.json.note: A real Twelve Data response, T1.1. Order as received: DESCENDING. Every one of its 20 price values is unchanged by a Number() round-trip, so it CANNOT detect a lost-precision bug - use twelvedata-decimal-guard.json for that.

twelvedata-xauusd-15min-ascending.json.note: The recorded response with values reversed into ascending order. Mechanical reversal, nothing else changed. Exists because the adapter requests order=ASC and asserts it, and the recorded response predates that parameter.

twelvedata-xauusd-15min-shuffled.json.note: POSITIVE CONTROL for assertAscending. Bars 1 and 2 of the ascending fixture are swapped. The ordering detector MUST reject this; if it passes, the detector is inert and every ordering test built on it proves nothing.

twelvedata-decimal-guard.json.note: POSITIVE CONTROL for ADR-008 decimal preservation. Every price and volume is a value that Number() round-tripping visibly changes (trailing zeros, and precision beyond float64). Verified mechanically when generated. This is the only fixture whose byte-equality assertion can actually fail.

twelvedata-error-429.json.note: NO TWELVE DATA ERROR RESPONSE HAS EVER BEEN OBSERVED BY THIS PROJECT. T1.1 recorded only successful calls. This body is written from vendor documentation, which this project treats as a starting point and not evidence. REPLACE WITH A RECORDED RESPONSE at T1.4 step 7. Tracked as OQ-3.

massive-xauusd-15min.json.note: T1.1 provider evaluation. Not used by the Twelve Data adapter.
